as_told.title: War of the Worlds broadcast panic

plain: The idea here is that the US government kept UFOs secret after the war partly because of how the public reacted to Orson Welles's 1938 radio play The War of the Worlds. Kurt McConnell, a Senate staffer, makes the point to Michels without citing a source. He says that in the late 1940s "we were barely, you know, a decade removed" from the broadcast, and he dates it to 1938. John S. Herrington, a former Secretary of Energy, gives the same reason on the show, speaking as a one-time official. He says that when Welles "broadcast War of the Worlds," the country "went nuts." Both use the memory of that panic to explain why officials kept quiet. If they are right, postwar secrecy about UFOs was driven less by the objects themselves than by fear of how Americans would react.
